content:
As a small project, a master student would like to formalize the axioms for reduced homology. In May's book A concise course of algebraic topology, these are defined as functors from the category of nondegenerately based spaces, i.e. the category pointed topological spaces (X, x) such that the inclusion {x} -> X is a cofibration.

I'm mainly wondering what is a good way of formalizing this last category. Should we have a category of pointed topological spaces, and get the desired one as the full subcategory? Maybe just use the slice under the point to get some instances for free? etc. Maybe @Joël Riou has ideas?

We have a formalization of Eilenberg-Steenrod axioms for pairs of topological spaces #38369 by @Jacob Scharmberg. I am not sure it would be a great idea to do something very similar.
Otherwise, it could be defined using an ObjectProperty for a suitable Under category.

From what I understand, having the reduced version is still useful, as e.g. it is more closely related to spectra via Brown's representability theorem. Admittedly, I don't know much about these topics, so if there is a nice way to bypass reduced homology I'd like to know.

For now, we will use the ObjectProperty and Under category approach, thanks!

This is actually a category of cofibrant objects:

module

public import Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Bifibrant

open CategoryTheory Limits

universe u

namespace HomotopicalAlgebra

variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasZeroObject C] [CategoryWithCofibrations C]
#synth Category (CofibrantObject C)

end HomotopicalAlgebra

When the dual construction of https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/ModelCategory/Over.html for Under categories is added, if we set up a (scoped) CategoryWithCofibrations TopCat.{u} instance, the category you are considering would be something like CofibrantObject (Under (TopCat.of PUnit.{u + 1})).
I defined a model category structure on topological spaces at https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category (it is not clear that the cofibrations are the same as May's though).
